# /crav1-pr-status

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From a pull request's threads: where it stands](../../from-pr-status.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-pr-status/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Show where one pull request stands, point by point, and who owes the next step.

**[`/crav1-pr-status`](crav1-pr-status.md)** reads one named pull request's threads, pushes and commits on Azure DevOps or GitHub (read-only, `references/pr-threads.md` in `crav1-add-to-spec`) and splits the threads into points. Each point gets one of six statuses: `done <sha>` (a commit after the request changed the lines), `agreed`, `declined` (with the reason), `open`, `waiting on <name>`, or `needs <name>` for a third person. It picks reviewer or author mode from who opened the pull request; `as reviewer` or `as author` overrides it, and an unclear sign-in is guessed without asking.

It prints a verdict line with the points waiting on you first, then the points by status, flags for threads resolved while the code is unchanged (and done points whose thread is still active), spec and decision candidates, follow-ups drafted for [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md), the pull requests this one depends on and the merge order, drafted replies, and a merge-readiness line. `since last` shows only what changed since your last run.

It writes all of it to the PR note's shared `## PR record`, the same record [`/crav1-review-pr`](crav1-review-pr.md), [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) and [`/crav1-merge-pr`](crav1-merge-pr.md) use; [`/crav1-merge-pr`](crav1-merge-pr.md) stops on `Ready: no`. Replies are drafts and are never posted. A thread status change on the host is offered one thread at a time and made only on that thread's yes. Spec or decision candidates go to [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) on a yes. Follow-ups are drafts; no work item is created.

1.98.0: also reads the pull request description: a `### Merge order` section becomes `Order` lines, `### Questions for reviewers` becomes Points tagged `asked; from description <date>`, and `### Not in this PR` is offered as follow-ups (a `follow-up` Point only on a yes). [`/crav1-open-pr`](crav1-open-pr.md) writes those sections.

## Choice words

Exact words for bots and scripted runs (no `--flags`). A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words.

| Question | Word | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which pull request | `pr<n>` | that pull request (also `pr <n>`, `#<n>`, `pr <repo> <n>`, or its URL) |
| Your side (optional; picked from the PR author otherwise) | `as reviewer` | reviewer mode: you are not the author |
| Your side (optional; picked from the PR author otherwise) | `as author` | author mode: you opened the pull request |
| How much | `since last` | only what changed since your last run |
| How much | `no code` | threads only; no diff or commit check, so nothing is marked done |

## Runs when

You want to know what is done and what is left on a pull request, and what you owe. Called by the user.

## Prompts

Prompt budget: 1 (the most prompts in one run, the closing yes included). A prompt may hold several questions. See the asking rule in `crav1.mdc`.

## Reads

In short: The pull request's threads, pushes and commits, its diff, and its PR record.

Reads one named pull request's threads with every comment, its pushes with their commits and changed files, the signed-in user, the diff of the source branch (unless `no code`), other pull requests named as merge-order dependencies, and the PR note with its `## PR record` in the specs repo.

## Writes

In short: The PR record in the PR note in `docs/notes/`; one thread status on the host per yes.

Writes the PR note's `## PR record` (a Point per point, Order, your Read line, Ready, State) and a `## Replies as drafted` history section, then regenerates the notes indexes; never committed. On a yes for that one thread, sets one thread's status on the host (Azure DevOps) or resolves or reopens it (GitHub).

## Does not

Leaves code, specs, plans, tasks and work items alone. Never posts a reply, votes, approves, merges, or changes a thread without its own yes.

Limits and exceptions: Signed out, the one prompt is the signed-out question and the offers are listed as text for the next run. Headless and bot runs ask nothing and list the offers as text.

## You run next / Runs by itself

- You run next: [`/crav1-merge-pr`](crav1-merge-pr.md); [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md); [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md); [`/crav1-review-pr`](crav1-review-pr.md)
- Runs by itself: Runs [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) with the spec and decision candidates only after a yes; calls no other skill.

## Lane and group

Lane: Cross-cutting. Group: Commit and pull request. Starter option: no. Routing: [guild routing](../../guild-routing.md).

## Stage and since

Stage: stable. Since: 1.97.0 ([changelog](../../../CHANGELOG.md)).
